name: Nunavut
summary: Gold and white vertical halves with a red inuksuk, a stone landmark, across the centre, and a blue star in the upper fly. It was introduced when Nunavut was created as a territory for the Inuit in 1999.
origin: Nunavut was separated from the Northwest Territories on 1 April 1999. Its flag and arms were designed through consultation with elders and communities and granted by the Governor General.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The riches of the land, sea and sky.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The riches of the land, sea and sky.

symbols.name: Inuksuk
symbols.meaning: The stone monuments that guide people on the land and mark sacred places.

symbols.name: North Star (Niqirtsuituq)
symbols.description: A blue star in the upper fly.
symbols.meaning: The traditional guide for navigation, and the leadership of elders.

facts: It is Canada's largest and least populated territory.
An inuksuk was also the logo of the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics.
clues: Gold and white halves with a red stone figure and a blue star.
Its stone figure is a traditional landmark of the Inuit.
The flag of a territory created in 1999.
